questions.set_intro: Imagine that a marketing firm is researching how people spend their free time in your area. You agreed to take part in a telephone interview about visiting museums.
questions.question: How often do you visit a museum, and what kind do you like most?
questions.model_answer: I visit a museum about once a month, usually on a weekend. I like history museums most, especially when the exhibits show ordinary objects from daily life.

questions.set_intro: Imagine that a marketing firm is researching how people spend their free time in your area. You agreed to take part in a telephone interview about visiting museums.
questions.question: Do you prefer going to a museum alone or with other people? Why?
questions.model_answer: I prefer going with one friend. We notice different details and can talk about them, but a large group usually moves too fast for me to enjoy the exhibits.

questions.set_intro: Imagine that a marketing firm is researching how people spend their free time in your area. You agreed to take part in a telephone interview about visiting museums.
questions.question: If a visitor had only one afternoon, what kind of museum would you recommend, and why?
questions.model_answer: I would recommend a city history museum to a visitor with one afternoon. It gives a clear sense of the place, and the main rooms can usually be seen in about two hours. I would tell the visitor to start with the oldest displays and to use a free audio guide if one is offered. That plan is a better use of a short visit than rushing through every gallery.

questions.question: Do you think a new employee should have a workplace mentor? Give reasons for your opinion.
questions.model_answer: I think a new employee should have a workplace mentor. A handbook rarely explains how one particular office really works, such as which tasks can wait or how people prefer to share updates. A mentor can answer those small questions in the first month, when a new person is most likely to feel lost. I saw this in a summer job. The colleague who showed me the filing system and introduced me at lunch made the second week much easier than the first. A mentor should not replace the manager, and it should be someone the new person can talk to honestly. With that support, people become useful faster and are more likely to stay. Even a few weeks of that guidance can prevent early mistakes.
